title: Microsoft Teams: events registration capacity rises to 20,000
summary: The registration limits and rollout window match Microsoft's notice, and the listed policy paths and commands are documented. Hold because the table reports no assignment automation even though Microsoft documents automation for Teams add-on licences through Microsoft Graph; the assignment path also stops before pack selection.

claims.claim: Teams events will support up to 20,000 registrations for organisers with valid attendee packs.
claims.quote: Connect with more attendees than ever before with Teams Events, now supporting up to 20,000 registrations for organizers with valid Attendee packs.

claims.claim: Registration capacity for town halls and webinars scales with event attendee capacity, up to 20,000 registrations.
claims.quote: Starting in December, registration capacity for Microsoft Teams town halls and webinars scales with the event's attendee capacity, up to 20,000 registrations per event.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Each organiser can be assigned only one attendee pack at a time.
claims.quote: Each organizer can only be assigned one attendee pack at a time. An organization can purchase multiple packs of varying sizes and assign them to different organizers.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Attendee Capacity Packs are add-on licences for Teams Enterprise that increase event attendee capacity beyond 3,000.
claims.quote: Teams Attendee Capacity Packs are add-on licenses for Teams Enterprise that let event organizers host events for up to 100,000 attendees.

claims.claim: Attendee pack sizes are 5K, 10K, 20K, 35K, 50K, 75K and 100K attendees.
claims.quote: They can be purchased to support 5,000, 10,000, 20,000, 35,000, 50,000, 75,000, and 100,000 event attendees.

claims.claim: Teams Enterprise capacity and a pack's capacity are not combined; a 20,000 pack gives 20,000 rather than 23,000 attendees.
claims.quote: The attendee capacities included with Teams Enterprise and an attendee pack aren't combined. For example, an organizer with a 20,000 attendee pack license can host events with engagement capabilities for up to 20,000 attendees (not 23,000).

claims.claim: Removing an attendee pack after scheduling can make upcoming events ineligible to run at their originally scheduled capacity.
claims.quote: If an attendee pack is removed after an event is scheduled, the upcoming event might no longer be eligible to run at the originally scheduled capacity.

claims.claim: Teams notifies the administrator when removal of a pack could disrupt upcoming events.
claims.quote: To reduce the risk of event disruption, Teams notifies both the admin and the organizer.

claims.claim: Teams also notifies the organiser when an attendee pack is removed.
claims.quote: The organizer receives an email notification that informs them the attendee pack was removed with a list of affected events.

claims.claim: Managing attendee pack licences in the Teams admin center requires the Global Administrator role.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Global Administrator role to access the License Management section and manage all licensing capabilities in the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: Teams Administrators have read-only access to License Management in the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: Users assigned the Teams Administrator role can access the License Management section in read-only mode and cannot create, modify, or remove license assignments or settings.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed: Teams Enterprise includes the lower registration capacity, with an add-on for higher capacity.
claims.quote: Organizers with Teams Enterprise can allow up to 3,000 registrations. Organizers with Attendee Capacity Packs can allow up to 20,000.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The capacity increase arrives without an administrator enabling it, represented by defaultState on.
claims.quote: No action is required. To prepare, you can:

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The pack assignment path is Teams admin center > Add-on Licenses > Teams Events > Licenses > Assign to new users.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, go to Add-on Licenses > Teams Events. On the Licenses tab, select Assign to new users to get started.
claims.fix: Extend controls[0].ui.path to 'Add-on Licenses > Teams Events > Licenses > Assign to new users > Assign Add-on licenses > Attendee pack'. The cited page says to select the organisers in the pane and select each user's pack size in the Attendee pack column; the existing path stops at the entry to that pane.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table; Open questions
claims.claim: No API or script is documented for assigning Attendee Capacity Packs.
claims.quote: You can use the Microsoft 365 admin center or PowerShell to assign licenses to users in your organization.
claims.fix: Replace controls[0].api null with kind 'graph', call 'POST /v1.0/users/{id}/assignLicense', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/user-assignlicense?view=graph-rest-1.0'. Add to the row note: 'The request body uses addLicenses with the purchased pack skuId; removeLicenses identifies licences to remove.' Cite that reference and https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/teams-add-on-licensing/assign-teams-add-on-licenses. Remove the Open questions bullet implying assignment automation is undocumented. The general Teams add-on assignment guide covers the licence class that the cited pack page explicitly places these packs in; absence from the pack-specific pages does not establish absence of automation.

claims.claim: Events up to 1,000 attendees are enabled through Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events up to 1k attendees.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Events policies. Select an existing policy or create a new one. For events with up to 1,000 attendees, such as webinars, turn the Events up to 1k attendees toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowWebinars Enabled enables creation of events up to 1,000 attendees for that policy.
claims.quote: To allow organizers with this policy to create events with up to 1,000 attendees, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowWebinars Enabled

claims.claim: Town hall-style events are enabled through Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Events optimized for a large audience.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Events policies. Select an existing policy or create a new one. For events optimized for large audiences, such as town halls, turn the Events optimized for a large audience toggle On or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Enabled enables creation of events optimised for large audiences.
claims.quote: To allow organizers with this policy to create events optimized for large audiences, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowTownhalls Enabled

claims.claim: Town hall attendee access is set through Teams admin center > Meetings > Events policies > policy > Who can attend events optimized for a large audience.
claims.quote: For events optimized for large audiences, such as town halls, in the Who can attend events optimized for a large audience dropdown list, select one of the following:

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallEventAttendeeAccess Everyone allows any user to attend large-audience events under that policy.
claims.quote: To allow any user to attend events optimized for large audiences created by organizers with this policy, run the following command: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -TownhallEventAttendeeAccess Everyone

claims.claim: EventAccessType is the corresponding attendance parameter for events up to 1,000 attendees.
claims.quote: For events with up to 1,000 attendees, such as webinars, use the -EventAccessType parameter.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The Learn pack pages publish no Attendee Capacity Pack price at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Attendee Capacity Pack price pricing registration charge 3000 20000. Read attendee-capacity-pack and attendee-capacity-pack-manage in full; both give sizes and licensing rules, but neither gives a monetary price.

claims.claim: A registration-specific charge is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Attendee Capacity Pack price pricing registration charge 3000 20000. Read both pack pages, the feature comparison and events-licensing search excerpts; none publishes a registration-specific charge.

claims.claim: No change to data access or destination is documented for this capacity increase.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams events 20000 registration capacity data storage compliance autonomous scheduling registration limit setting. Read MC1557760 ('No compliance considerations identified'), pack pages and feature comparison; none describes a new data access or destination for this increase.

claims.claim: No autonomous behaviour is described for this registration-capacity increase.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams events 20000 registration capacity data storage compliance autonomous scheduling registration limit setting. Read MC1557760, pack pages and Plan for Teams events scheduling passages; none describes autonomous behaviour for the increase.

claims.claim: The organiser sets event capacity in the event scheduling form.
claims.quote: Event capacity isn't automatically updated when a larger capacity attendee pack is assigned. The organizer must manually update the event capacity in the event scheduling form.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Existing Teams events policies govern who can schedule and attend events.
claims.quote: This article describes how you, as an admin, can manage which users can create and attend events in your organization.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified how the existing up-to-1,000-attendee toggle governs the newly announced large webinars with registration.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams webinar town hall registration capacity limit admin setting policy 20000 AllowWebinars. Read set-up-events and Plan for Teams events: they describe attendee-count/optimisation rules, not MC1557760's new non-broadcast large-registration webinar case.

claims.claim: No separate administrator setting for the numeric registration limit is documented in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams webinar town hall registration capacity limit admin setting policy 20000 AllowWebinars. Read set-up-events, manage-registration-form-events and Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy. Registration enables/disables registration and is documented as having no effect; none sets a numeric limit.

claims.claim: The Teams Events page in the Teams admin center shows purchased pack stock and current assignments.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, go to Add-on Licenses > Teams Events. On the Teams Events page, you see your organization's attendee pack inventory, including available attendee packs that you purchased and current assignments.

claims.claim: The Usage reports tab on the Teams Events page shows how attendee packs are used across the organisation.
claims.quote: On the Usage reports tab of the Teams Events page, you can monitor how attendee packs are used across your organization.

claims.claim: The event inventory lets administrators review events affected by pack removal.
claims.quote: In the event inventory, admins can view the list of affected events.
